question: In Mendel's experiments, when he crossed a tall (TT) pea plant with a short (tt) pea plant, what did he observe in the first generation (F1)?

options.text: Half of them were tall, and the other half were short.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Everything was tall.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Gregor Mendel, the "Father of Genetics," conducted experiments on **pea plants** to study the inheritance of traits.
 
• In this specific experiment, Mendel crossed a **pure tall plant (TT)** with a **pure short plant (tt)**.
 
• The resulting first-generation (F1) offspring were all **tall plants**. This phenomenon occurs because the tall trait is **dominant**, while the short trait is **recessive**.
 
• The genetic makeup (genotype) of the F1 generation was **Tt**, but the physical appearance (phenotype) was tall.
 
• This observation confirmed Mendel's principle of **dominance**, which states that in a heterozygous condition, the dominant allele masks the expression of the recessive allele.
